chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The mukatab (slave who has contracted for manumission upon paying a sum) is not permitted to have emancipation, nor gift, nor marriage, nor testimony, nor pilgrimage, until he pays all that is upon him. If his master stipulated that if he were unable to pay one installment, he would be returned to slavery.

key_terms.اَلْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has contracted to buy their freedom by paying a lump sum or installments to the master.
key_terms.رَدٌّ فِي الرِّقِّ: Returned to slavery / reverted to slavery.

ai.seo_question: What are the legal restrictions on a mukatab slave before full payment of their manumission contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the legal restrictions on the mukatab, a slave under a manumission contract, prohibiting acts like marriage, testimony, and pilgrimage until the full debt is settled. It further validates the master's stipulation that missing any single installment results in a reversion to slavery, highlighting the conditional nature of their freedom. This ruling underscores the balance between the slave's progress toward liberty and the master's financial security within Shia jurisprudence.
